title: Add residency enforcement dashboards + alert rules (violations + policy-evaluator health)
author: Sergio Costa
description:
Context: Hosted data residency enforcement is rolling out in canary/beta and SRE needs first-class visibility + actionable alerting. This PR adds Grafana dashboard panels and Prometheus alert rules for (1) residency violations and (2) policy-evaluator health, plus links to the operational runbook for fast triage.

What’s included: New Grafana dashboard: “Data Residency Enforcement” (overview) with panels for violation rate, top orgs/projects, decision breakdown, and routing-related signals. New alert rules: residency violation spike (per org + global), policy-evaluator error budget burn / elevated 5xx, policy decision latency regression, and missing metrics (scrape/ingest) for the enforcement path. All alerts include runbook_url annotations and consistent label keys (region, env, org_tier where available). Dashboard uses the metrics introduced in redwood PR #18473 and assumes the gateway emits decision labels (allow/deny) and requested/enforced region tags.

Out of scope: any new instrumentation. This PR strictly consumes existing metrics/log-derived series; missing series will show as N/A until redwood PRs land in the same environment.

Rollout: safe to deploy everywhere; alerts are shipped disabled by default in prod via env overrides (enabled in staging + canary). This matches the residency enforcement rollout plan to avoid noisy pages during early beta.

Runbook: Confluence runbook link is included in alert annotations and dashboard links: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/runbook-residency-violation-spike (owner: SRE + Platform).

Testing: rendered dashboards via grafonnet compile; validated alert rules with promtool; verified in staging against synthetic violation traffic.

Checklist: [x] promtool test passes [x] dashboard JSON renders in Grafana [x] alert annotations include runbook_url + summary [x] staging validation screenshots attached in internal comment [x] labels follow observability-pack conventions
commits: dashboards: add data-residency-enforcement overview dashboard (grafonnet + rendered json)
alerts: add residency violation spike + policy-evaluator health rule groups
mixins: standardize runbook_url + service labels for residency-related alerts
docs: add dashboard/alert index entry and ownership metadata
chore: tighten promql recording rules and fix lint for annotation templates
conversation:
Allison Grant (review): PromQL looks good overall. Two nits: (1) please add an explicit panel for denominator traffic (total enforcement checks) so violation rate spikes can be interpreted; (2) runbook_url should be under annotations not labels, to avoid cardinality mistakes.

Sergio Costa (author): Added “Residency checks / sec” panel in the top row and moved runbook_url into annotations for all rules. Also aligned with templating.libsonnet helper so we don’t regress.

Sean Gallagher (review): For the global violation spike alert, can we gate it to only fire when total checks > X to avoid canary noise? Also what’s the intended severity during beta?

Sergio Costa (author): Added traffic gate (sum(rate(residency_checks_total[5m])) > 2) and set severity=warning by default, with env override to critical once GA. Not enabling in prod by default.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please link to the specific runbook section for ‘policy evaluator down’ in the policy-evaluator alert group. And can you add an alert for “policy evaluator cache stale / decision latency p95”?

Sergio Costa (author): Added anchor links in the runbook URLs (policy-evaluator section) and included a p95 latency alert for policy evaluation. The cache-stale symptom is tricky; I added a missing-metrics + elevated decision latency signal to cover this operationally.

Logan Wright (review): Dashboard: can we include breakdown by org_tier and by pinned_region? The metrics emitted by gateway include org_tier label only in canary right now.

Sergio Costa (author): Added optional breakdown panels; they’ll show “no data” until label is present. Kept them below the fold to avoid confusion.

Allison Grant (final): Approving. Thanks for keeping prod alerts disabled-by-default; this will prevent paging during the first cohort.

Sean Gallagher (final): Approved. Please make sure the alert routing policy in PagerDuty is updated when we enable in prod.

Sergio Costa (author): Will coordinate with ENG-2849 rollout checklist; added note in CHANGELOG and docs catalog.
release_notes: Observability Pack: Added “Data Residency Enforcement” dashboard and alert rule groups for residency violations and policy-evaluator health. Alerts include runbook links and are disabled-by-default in prod pending residency enforcement GA.
